subject: Starlite production latency after model roll
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@starlite.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@starlite.ai
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High P99 after today's model rollout (canary -> prod)

Hey Marcus / Marissa,

We started seeing a large uptick in p95/p99 latency this morning coincident with the canary roll of model v2.3.1 to production. Key metrics from our side (US east):
- p95 went from ~220ms to ~480ms over the last 2 hours
- p99 spiked from ~480ms to 1.9s and some requests are timing out (504)
- Error rate (5xx) has climbed from 0.1% to ~3.7%

We captured a short sample of request traces and stack snapshots attached (perf-sample-logs.zip). Grafana link shows the spike: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/starlite-p99

This is affecting transactions for paying users — we have some revenue impact already. Can you urgently confirm whether Redwood rolled a config or model variant that would affect latency for long context or batching behavior? If a quick rollback to previous model/variant is possible, please advise and schedule.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Infrastructure
Starlite AI

--
Attachment: perf-sample-logs.zip (zip, 2.3MB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@starlite.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High P99 after today's model rollout (canary -> prod)

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the sample logs. Marissa/Connor/Team: can we triage immediately?

Initial ask:
- Confirm whether Starlite was routed to any new model variant or quantized family in the last 6 hours.
- Check canary -> prod rollout status (which nodes were flipped) and whether any autoscaler/batching policy changed.
- If we see consistent p99 regression in the canary, prepare a rollback plan to the previous model build and a communication template for Starlite.

Connor — can you lead telemetry (queue times, GPU wait, KV-cache hit rate) and post the first findings here. Marissa — can you validate any recent runtime/kernel selection changes for the model family? Lauren — tag ops/partner success for credits and contractual impact if SLA triggers.

I will loop in leadership if this becomes broad. Marcus
Senior PM, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@starlite.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High P99 after today's model rollout (canary -> prod)

Adding what I see from the runtime side after a quick pass:
- The canary roll targeted the v2.3.1 checkpoint plus a new kernel selection that optimized for throughput at longer prompts. That kernel path increases attention workspace allocations by ~15% (seen in the canary profile).
- For Starlite's default traffic pattern (many short requests but occasional long contexts), the new kernel increases memory pressure and causes queuing on some GPU hosts under burst.
- KV-cache hit rate for Starlite is unchanged; batching rate increased slightly because the runtime tried to aggregate small requests into larger pipelines.

Attached is a small profile from the canary host (canary-profile.txt). I recommend immediate rollback of the kernel selection for the Starlite route (not necessarily the whole model) while we investigate the queuing behavior. If we can toggle routing policy to use the previous kernel for Starlite only, that should be lower risk.

Marissa
Lead SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: canary-profile.txt (text, 45KB)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@starlite.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High P99 after today's model rollout (canary -> prod)

Quick telemetry snapshot: see Grafana link for full panels. TL;DR: GPU queue time (avg) jumped from ~12ms -> 250ms on the subset of hosts that served the canary. P99 queue time correlates with the p99 observed by Starlite.

Evidence:
- Host group g-n1 (canary) shows sustained GPU scheduler backlog starting 08:40 UTC.
- Preemption events: none. Memory used per model instance jumped ~14%.
- Batching: runtime attempted larger batches during tail traffic; this amplified latency for short requests (head-of-line problem).

Action I initiated:
- I set a route override to reduce max batch size for Starlite to minimize batching-induced HOL latency (temporary).
- Preparing a rollback playbook to revert the kernel selection for their route. See: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/rollback-canary

Recommendation: full rollback of kernel selection for Starlite route ASAP. If rollback timeline > 30m, propose a model routing fallback to v2.3.0 for Starlite while we debug.

Connor
Infra Lead
Redwood Inference

--
Related dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/starlite-p99
From: Elena Soto <elena@starlite.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 10:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High P99 after today's model rollout (canary -> prod)

Thanks for the quick reaction.
We need rollback to the prior stable path immediately. Our customers are experiencing timeouts; engineering is seeing retries increase. If there's a chance to throttle back batching or route to v2.3.0 we will take it now.

Also please note our contract includes a credit trigger at 99.5% SLA — if this persists into the billing window we'll expect credit calculations.

Elena

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@starlite.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: Starlite latency regression (requesting exec awareness)

Hannah/Lauren — looping you in due to customer impact and SLA risk. Starlite (SL-2024-119) is seeing p99 regressions after a kernel selection change that was rolled in the canary. Internal telemetry shows GPU queue backlog on the canary nodes, and we have a customer request for immediate rollback/fallback.

Current actions:
- Connor has applied a temporary route override to reduce batch size.
- Marissa recommends toggling kernel selection back for the Starlite route; Connor is preparing rollback steps.
- I want approval to execute a per-account rollback (route-level) now. If leadership prefers, we can do a staged rollback: (1) per-account kernel toggle; (2) if unresolved, global rollback for that model family.

Customer asks: rollback to previous path ASAP and SLA credit calc if we dip below threshold. I will coordinate the customer comms and credit calculation with Lauren.

We should aim to have rollback executed within the next 30 minutes. Marcus
Senior PM, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@starlite.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 00:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation: Starlite latency regression (requesting exec awareness) — ROLLBACK COMPLETE

Update and resolution summary:
- 2026-07-19 23:15 UTC: performed route-level toggle to previous kernel selection for Starlite traffic (v2.3.0 kernel path).
- 2026-07-19 23:40 UTC: observed p95/p99 return to baseline in US-east for Starlite. p99 now ~510ms, p95 ~210ms. Error rate reduced to ~0.15%.
- Attached: rollback-report-20260720.txt (contains timestamps and hosts affected).

Immediate next steps: postmortem scheduled for Tuesday 07/21 10:00 UTC; root-cause will cover kernel selection heuristics and batching heuristics for mixed short/long prompt workloads. Connor will lead corrective runtime changes to avoid HOL batching in similar routes. Lauren will calculate SLA impact and proposed customer credit.

Elena — apologies for the disruption. We will send a formal account note and the postmortem after internal review.

Marissa
Lead SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
